turns.t: Doctor, I'm worried about my heart rhythm, and I'm on warfarin for it. I want to make sure I'm doing everything right.
That's a good reason to come. Tell me how you've been feeling.
Every now and then my heart flutters, like a bird in my chest. It lasts a few minutes.
How often does that happen?
Maybe once or twice a week.
Any dizziness, chest pain, or fainting with it?
No chest pain. No fainting. I do feel a bit breathless sometimes.
How is the breathlessness? When does it happen?
When I climb the stairs, mostly. It settles after a rest.
Good to know. Tell me about the warfarin. What dose are you on? ~
Warfarin 3 mg, once a day in the evening.
Any missed doses, or bleeding, like nosebleeds or bruising?
No bleeding. I've not missed a dose.
Thank you. When was your last INR blood test? ~
Three weeks ago. The nurse said it was in range. ~
Do you have any allergies to medicines?
I'm allergic to sulfa drugs. I got a rash with them years ago.
Noted. Do you drink alcohol?
One or two glasses of wine a week.
Good. Now, with your fluttering and breathlessness, I'd like to record your heart over a few days.
How do you do that? ~
You wear a small monitor, a Holter, for forty-eight hours, and it records every heartbeat.
Will I be able to shower? ~
Not with the monitor on, but you can wash around it. I'll arrange it for next week.
And what about the blood test? ~
I'd like to repeat the INR in two weeks, because small changes in diet can move it.
Right. Should I change anything in my diet? ~
Keep your green vegetables steady rather than stopping them, and tell me about any new medicines. ~
I will. ~
The new plan is to keep the warfarin as it is for now, and we'll decide after the monitor. ~
Thank you, doctor. That puts my mind at rest. ~
